parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal binary passport/entry rules, federal facility exclusion and documented immigration-custody abuse create real traveller exposure that state law does not cancel, but the state provides operative public-accommodations, hate-crime, restroom and sanctuary/care protections with no local facility ban. Likely outcome for an outed adult visitor is entry friction, refusal or federal-facility exclusion, not imprisonment or execution; for a minor, federal school/care hostility is partly mitigated locally by sanctuary and care-access laws. Two 2026 killings in one city, perpetrator at large, add street risk but no denominator to assess background rate. Net: elevated-to-reduced risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary definition, X-marker passports stopped Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility if wilful misrepresentation suspected.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic; state IDs allow X and birth-certificate change without surgery, but do not govern federal entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger secondary screening, refusal and fraud consideration at federal entry; state ID protections do not pre-empt federal adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented state prisoner-placement rule, unit or case; federal/national custody governed nationally, not by state.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detention follows entry, investigation or other offence, federal custody exposure overrides state's protective laws; state custody placement is unresolved, not documented as safe.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; 21 states/provinces have some bans nationally, though this state is among 33 with no mapped ban locally.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State nondiscrimination law since 2014 covers public accommodations; 2018 court ruling protects trans students using restrooms/locker rooms consistent with identity; county gender-neutral options exist.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities are protected locally, but federal buildings, military and other federal settings remain restricted; traveller must plan by operator, not only city.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and proposed rules restrict gender-affirming care for minors and public reimbursement under 18; DOJ subpoenas and funding threats nationally; airport screening can out travellers and disrupt medication access.
care_services.protection: State 2023 executive order protects unimpeded access, 2024 insurance law described as most trans healthcare friendly, public programme covers surgery for eligible residents over 18 from Jan 2024.
care_services.interaction: State sanctuary/care protections help an adult visitor seek local care, but whether sanctuary extends to non-residents is not sourced; federal minor-care hostility remains for federal programmes and travel across state lines.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal policy frames gender identity as binary, removes gender-ideology materials, military ban, trans athletes entry ban, counterterrorism strategy mentioning radically pro-transgender groups; public opinion 66% supports assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law adds penalties for gender-identity bias since 2021, gay/trans panic defence abolished, 2024 sanctuary law passed 33-13 and 97-38.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State protections operate in state policing, housing and accommodations, but federal law-enforcement priorities and federal facilities/entry are not displaced by state sanctuary status on this record.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal 2025 orders direct investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns, ban care for minors in 27 states nationally, and bar trans athletes from women's competition entry.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy on minors since 2018, court protects student restroom access, athletes may participate by gender identity without proof per 2022 county report, sanctuary law protects care access.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor-parent pair faces federal school/sport/care hostility if using federal systems, but state schools and clinics described as protective; sanctuary coverage for non-resident minors is uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Sept 2026 Black trans woman shot dead in largest city, second Black trans woman shot in that city within ten weeks, perpetrator at large; no general homicide denominator supplied, so excess over background is not established.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalties, LGBTIQ+ commission, county bill of rights, and analysis places state in safest law/incident band, though rankings lack per-capita denominator.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Pattern of two killings in ten weeks raises concern for visibly trans visitors in that city, but without background rate it cannot be treated as proven trans-specific campaign; state recourse exists on paper.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved, several orders blocked/enjoined, exposure depends on measures in effect at travel time; no per-capita violence data, no state custody rule, sanctuary visitor scope unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National hate-crime statute, state nondiscrimination and sanctuary laws, ACLU-type legal aid FAQ documented nationally, state commission and courts have ruled for trans students.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are fragmented across federal/state courts and may not be timely for a short-stay visitor facing entry refusal, eviction from a federal facility, or detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: exclusion there is universal, routine and without effective remedy. Here entry refusal/fraud risk exists federally, but state public-accommodations, hate-crime and sanctuary protections operate locally and fraud ineligibility is not automatic, so materially safer.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening, possible refusal/return transport, slow appeals, but administrative rather than criminal outcome. This case adds stronger state protections than 0.55-B, offset by severe documented federal custody abuse if detained.

Higher than 0.75-C: that anchor has respectful border training, brief detention only and working tribunal compensation. Here federal binary policy, transp athlete ban and custody abuse create heavier, less predictable exposure despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two sovereigns: federal entry, passport, federal facilities and detention are hostile and can produce refusal, outing, or in custody severe abuse; the state counters with operative nondiscrimination, hate-crime, restroom, care and sanctuary protections and no local facility ban. State law mitigates everyday street, lodging, school and clinic exposure but does not documentedly cancel federal screening, federal facilities or immigration custody. The final interaction—discrepancy at entry leading toward refusal/fraud consideration, or any detention leading to federal custody—is the governing risk, hence below Reduced-Risk anchors but well above regimes with imprisonment/execution.
